docs.title: Frame extraction
docs.text: Use Frame Extractor to choose and extract frames from videos into your project.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• A project only needs a config.yaml file.
  • If you already have images, you can skip frame extraction:
  • Create an images folder next to config.yaml.
  • Copy image files into images.

When you run Junip3R and select a config.yaml file, the frame extractor opens automatically if no images are found in images.

docs.title: Add videos
docs.text:
You can add videos in two ways:

  • Drag and drop video files into the app.
  • Click Add Videos and select files in the file explorer.

docs.title: Select frames
docs.text: Frames can be selected manually or automatically.

docs.title: Manual selection
docs.text:
1. Double-click a video in the video list to open it in the center player.
  2. Navigate with play/pause, the seek bar, or frame-by-frame arrow buttons.
  3. Click Select Frame to add the currently displayed frame.

docs.title: Automatic selection
docs.text:
In the frame selection menu (under the video list), choose:

  • Strategy: random or kmeans
  • How many frames to select
  • Selection mode:
  • total across videos
  • per video
  • Video scope:
  • all videos
  • currently displayed videos
  • videos selected in the video list

Click Select Frames to run the selection.

docs.title: Random strategy
docs.text:
• n total frames: selects n frames from all frames across all included videos.
  • Every frame has equal probability, even when video lengths differ.
  • n per video: selects n frames randomly, from each included video.

docs.title: KMeans strategy
docs.text:
For selecting frames that are as diverse as possible

  • n total frames:
  • Runs KMeans with n clusters on all frames from all included videos.
  • Frames are downscaled to 8x8 for clustering.
  • Selects the n frames closest to the cluster centroids.
  • n per video:
  • Runs KMeans with n clusters separately for each included video.

docs.title: Extract selected frames
docs.text:
After selecting frames, use the frame extraction menu (under the frame list) to choose what to extract:

  • New frames
  • Extracts only frames that have not been extracted before.
  • All frames
  • Extracts all frames, even if they have been extracted before, replacing existing files.
  • Frames selected in the frame list
  • Extracts only the frames that are selected in the frame list.

You can also enable context clip extraction and set the context length in seconds on both sides of each frame.

  • Example: 2s context creates a 4s clip (2s before + 2s after).

Click Extract Frames to export.

docs.title: Output locations
docs.text:
• Extracted frames are saved to images (next to config.yaml).
  • Context clips are saved to context.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Junip3R can be installed in two ways:

  1. Use the portable executable from the latest GitHub release (no Python setup needed).
  2. Install as a Python package from GitHub and run it with the junip3r command.

docs.title: Option 1: Portable executable (ZIP)
docs.text:
Latest release: https://github.com/ETHZ-3Rhub/Junip3R/releases/latest

  1. Open the latest release page on GitHub.
  2. Download the ZIP file that contains the Windows executable.
  3. Extract the ZIP to any folder.
  4. Run Junip3R.exe.

This installation is self-contained and does not require a separate Python installation. The Junip3R.exe file must always be located next to the _internal folder.

docs.title: Option 2: Install from GitHub as a package
docs.text: Repository: https://github.com/ETHZ-3Rhub/Junip3R

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or newer
  • pip

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/ETHZ-3Rhub/Junip3R.git"

If you are installing from a specific branch:

python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/ETHZ-3Rhub/Junip3R.git@<branch-name>"

Or a specific release:

python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/ETHZ-3Rhub/Junip3R.git@<release-version>"

docs.title: Run
docs.text: junip3r

docs.title: Verify installation
docs.text:
• Portable install: the app opens when you run Junip3R.exe.
  • Package install: the app opens when you run junip3r in a terminal.

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
Portable install: Download the latest release from GitHub and replace the existing version.

Package install:

python -m pip install --upgrade "git+https://github.com/ETHZ-3Rhub/Junip3R.git"

docs.title: Labelling workflow
docs.text: Use the Labeller to create and edit instances, points, and bounding boxes for each image.

docs.title: Opening the Labeller
docs.text:
• When you start Junip3R and select a config.yaml file, the Labeller opens if image files are present in images.
  • From the Frame Extractor, open it by clicking Start Labelling.

docs.title: First state when the Labeller opens
docs.text:
• The first image is loaded from images (alphabetical order).
  • In the instance list, Add new instance is selected by default.
  • If instances (expected instance types) are defined in config.yaml, the first expected type is preselected.
  • If no expected list is defined, the first configured instance type is selected.

docs.title: Creating and deleting instances
docs.text:
When Add new instance is selected:

  • A new instance is created automatically when you place its first point or bounding box.
  • The new instance uses the type shown in the instance type dropdown.
  • The instance receives a name and becomes the selected instance.

An instance is deleted automatically when its last point is deleted.

You can also delete an entire instance by selecting it in the instance list and pressing the Delete key.

docs.title: Point and type progression
docs.text:
• After placing a point, selection advances to the next point of the same instance.
  • After placing the last point of an instance, selection moves to Add new instance again.
  • If expected instances are configured, the type dropdown advances to the next expected type.

Placing the next point then creates a new instance of that currently selected type.

docs.title: Selecting and changing instances
docs.text:
• Select any instance or point from the instance and point lists.
  • While Add new instance is selected, you can change the type for the next instance in the type dropdown.
  • If expected instances are configured, manual type changes are usually only needed when an expected instance is missing in the current frame.
  • After a manual type change, automatic type selection tries to continue following the expected list for later instances.

When an existing instance is selected, you can also change its type in the dropdown. If the new type has fewer points, extra points at the end are removed.

docs.title: Points
docs.text:
• Place a point: left-click on the image.
  • Move a point: drag with left mouse button.
  • Delete a point: right-click the point.

docs.title: Bounding boxes
docs.text:
• Place a box: left-click once for the first corner, then left-click again for the opposite corner.
  • Delete a box: right-click inside the box area (but not on a point).
  • Move a box: not supported.
  • Replace a box: select it in the point list and place the two corners again.

docs.title: Undo and redo
docs.text:
• Undo: Ctrl+Z
  • Redo: Ctrl+Y

Undo/redo history is tracked per image.

docs.title: Image navigation
docs.text:
• Use Next and Previous buttons.
  • Or use Left Arrow and Right Arrow keys.
  • Jump to any image with the image slider.

docs.title: Saving and output
docs.text:
• All changes are saved automatically.
  • For each image, a matching JSON label file is written to labels (next to images).

docs.title: Project Setup
docs.text:
To start a new project, create an empty folder with a config.yaml file.

When you run Frame Extractor on this folder, Junip3R creates the remaining project structure automatically.

docs.title: Minimum required config.yaml
docs.text:
At minimum, define instance_types. Each instance type needs:

  • name: unique instance type name
  • points: list of point names for that instance type
instance_types:
- name: mouse_top
  points:
  - nose
  - headcentre
  - neck
  - earl
  ...

docs.title: Optional fields
docs.text: See docs/Examples/advanced_config.yaml) for more details

docs.title: Per instance type
docs.text:
• bounding_box_type: automatic or manual (default is manual)
  • automatic: box is computed tightly around points
  • manual: user places the box manually
  • skeleton: list of point pairs, for example [[nose, headcentre], [headcentre, neck]]
  • colors: list of hex colors for points (same order as points)
  • box_color: hex color for the bounding box
  • skeleton_color: hex color for skeleton lines

docs.title: Project-wide
docs.text:
• instances: ordered list of expected instance type names
  • Used by the UI to auto-select the next type while labelling

docs.text:

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text: This page walks through the fastest path from installation to labelled data.

docs.title: 1) Install and launch Junip3R
docs.text:
Install Junip3R (portable ZIP or Python package), then start the app.

  • See: Installation

docs.title: 2) Create a new project folder
docs.text:
1. Create an empty folder for your project.

  2. Add a config.yaml file with at least one instance type and point list.

  3. See: Project Setup

  4. Example config files: docs/Examples/minimal_config.yaml, docs/Examples/advanced_config.yaml

docs.title: 3) Open the project
docs.text:
Start Junip3R and select your config.yaml file.

  • If images already contains image files, the Labeller opens directly.
  • If no images are present, Frame Extractor opens.

docs.title: Path A: Extract from videos in Frame Extractor
docs.text:
1. Add videos.
  2. Select frames manually or automatically.
  3. Click Extract Frames.

  4. Click Start Labelling.

  5. See: Frame extraction

docs.title: Path B: Use existing images
docs.text:
1. Create an images folder next to config.yaml.
  2. Copy your image files into images.
  3. Open config.yaml in Junip3R.

docs.title: 5) Label your data
docs.text:
1. Place points and bounding boxes.
  2. Navigate through images and continue labelling.

  3. Changes are saved automatically to labels as JSON.

  4. See: Labelling workflow

docs.title: 6) Export
docs.text:
When labelling is complete, export in your target format.

  • See: Exporting

docs.title: Exporting
docs.text: Junip3R can export project data as a YOLO training dataset.

docs.title: Open the export dialog
docs.text:
In the Labeller, open:

File -> Export as... -> YOLO Training Dataset

docs.title: Choose the target folder
docs.text:
• In the YOLO export dialog, click the folder button next to Target Folder.
  • Select the folder where the dataset should be created.

docs.title: Choose how to split the dataset
docs.text:
Use the Train/Val split by: dropdown to choose how data is grouped:

  • Video: all images from the same video stay in the same set
  • Image: each image is assigned independently

Use the slider below the dropdown to choose how many videos or images go into each set.

docs.title: Choose which instance types to include
docs.text:
In the instance type list, enable or disable types using the checkboxes.

Only checked instance types are included in the exported dataset.

docs.title: Export the dataset
docs.text:
Click Export to generate the YOLO dataset.

The export uses the selected split settings and writes the dataset to the target folder.

docs.title: Reusing an existing split
docs.text:
The exported dataset includes a set_split.txt file that records which images or videos were assigned to each set.

If you open the export dialog again and select the same target folder:

  • the existing split is loaded automatically
  • the same images or videos stay in the same sets
  • this helps keep training results consistent and comparable

If new images or videos have been added, you can use the slider to assign the new items as well.

If everything is already assigned, the slider is replaced with the message:

set is already fully split

docs.title: Using a split from another dataset folder
docs.text:
When exporting to a different target folder, you can still reuse an older split.

  • Click the file button next to Existing split file:
  • Select the set_split.txt file from an existing dataset folder

This applies the same split layout to the new export.
